text:
Original J, A = P7, and B = P9 remain distinct historical occurrences. I do not overwrite J or treat the supplied criticism as an installed repair. What follows is a proposed successor, J′, to one part of J: the aggregation claim about the independent per-booking min/max interval and its relation to compatibility. J′ is a new artifact, not an amendment to C0 or to either candidate language.

## Assessment of the criticism

The criticism warrants a change, but only to J’s aggregation paragraph and its proposed remedy. J says the independent min/max interval is the availability object “only under” an added assumption that all combinations of local alternatives are compatible, and it proposes either adding a compatibility relation/resource model or weakening the claim to “bounds under independence.”

That is too narrow. The interval is at best a bound. Even if all combinations of local alternatives are compatible, the set of possible totals can fail to be an interval because sums of discrete alternatives can be non-convex or have holes. The criticism’s distinguishing case is valid: two bookings with alternatives `{0, 10}`, capacity 15, all combinations compatible, gives possible availabilities `{15, 5, -5}`, while the independent min/max interval is `[-5, 15]`. Availability 0 is in the interval but not achievable. So compatibility is not sufficient for the interval to be the exact availability object. It is also not the only possible gap between bounds and exactness.

J’s core classification still survives, however. P9’s compatibility objection is still best read in P7’s terms as a criticism of an aggregation rule and a sufficiency assumption, with unresolved ambiguity about whether the snapshot as a whole is blamed. The change is that compatibility is one possible missing condition among others, not the sole condition.

## Proposed successor J′

> P9’s compatibility objection is not primarily a criticism of a record, a booking history, or the supersession rule. It targets the aggregation step by which local alternatives are turned into a global availability claim, and a sufficiency assumption about what the snapshot names. In P7’s terms, the target is a reconstruction rule and a source assumption, with unresolved ambiguity about whether the snapshot as a whole is blamed.
>
> The useful distinction is between target, remedy, and sufficiency assumption, plus a further distinction between a bound and an exact availability object. P9’s local material gives per-booking possibility sets: reservations may be unresolved among tied greatest-revision active holds. The global sum is not well-defined when alternatives remain. The independent per-booking minima and maxima give lower and upper bounds on availability. Those bounds are not the exact set of possible availabilities; they are projections that may include values no joint selection can produce. The exact object, if one is claimed, is the set of availability values induced by selections from the per-booking alternatives together with any cross-booking compatibility relation.
>
> P9’s correlation objection says cross-booking incompatibility is one way the interval can fail to be exact: booking A’s high alternative might be incompatible with booking B’s high alternative if they share a physical resource not named in the snapshot. This is a conditional possibility, not an observation, and P9 notes that the snapshot does not name physical resources. But compatibility is not the only issue. Even if all combinations are compatible, the possible totals can be non-convex or discrete, so the interval can contain unachievable availabilities. Therefore an account that claims its interval or single number is exhaustive global availability needs both (i) a representation of the jointly possible selections/totals, not merely an interval, and (ii) any compatibility/resource relation. An account that claims only bounds need not be revised by P9; it should label them as bounds under independence, and it still does not thereby become exact.
>
> If negative availability is allowed as a valid over-reservation, capacity alone is not a hard incompatibility relation, so the needed compatibility relation is not simply “sum ≤ capacity.” That remains disputed.
>
> A discriminating question: For account G, does its global availability object claim exactness or only bounds? If exact, does G represent the possible total set and any compatibility relation? Does that representation exclude any combination included by the independent interval? If yes, P9’s objection is internal to G. If no, P9’s objection is not yet a criticism of G. If G claims only bounds, P9’s objection is met by explicit labeling. Additional observations that would matter are a resource model, an allocation trace showing incompatible combinations, or a downstream requirement for a single number. None is in the frozen packet.

## Effect on the proposed organization and remaining protected uses

The criticized distinction changes the organization by separating three things that J partly fused: the gap due to cross-booking compatibility, the gap due to non-convexity or discreteness of possible totals, and the difference between a bound and an exact availability object. Compatibility becomes one possible limitation, not the only missing relation. The remedy splits accordingly: an exactness claim requires a representation of jointly possible selections or totals; a bounds claim requires only explicit labeling as bounds.

These protected uses remain:

- Questioning a rule remains distinct from questioning a record.
- Accepting or rejecting a rule and accepting or rejecting data remain independent combinations.
- The cross-booking incompatibility in P9 remains a conditional possibility, not an observation.
- Local alternatives, global aggregation, bounds, and correlation objections remain different roles.
- The dispute about retaining uncertainty and the objection to pushing resolution downstream remain disputed positions, not resolved facts.
- Negative availability and whether capacity is a hard constraint remain unresolved.
- The E009 criticism’s proposed repairs remain proposals, not installed facts or evidence about the warehouse.

Any language extension—such as adding a compatibility-relation primitive or a possible-worlds layer—is a separate proposed object, not an installed part of the frozen carrier. The current prose route can carry the distinction without making Lean or RSS obligatory. This successor may itself be false or incomplete; it is offered as a proposed successor, not as an executed repair.
